title: Set the trip
narration: This is a new, live Survive Drive session. I am setting a Santa Clarita start and a Long Beach destination. The map and route candidates are still empty, so you can follow the search from its first click.

title: Review road preferences
narration: Before searching, I review the Valhalla road controls. Highway and toll preferences stay at their neutral defaults for this example. We can change them here, but the new search would then need its own route and evidence review.

title: Build the escape gates
narration: I request four suggested escape gates near each end of the trip. The circles and road suggestions appear in the app itself. With the no-gate choice on both ends, four gates each way create five times five, or twenty five, start and destination pairings.

title: Search all pairings
narration: The local Valhalla server now searches those twenty five pairings. It returns twenty seven distinct route candidates. This is real route data for this session; no property lookup was needed to make the routes.

title: Read Round Zero
narration: Round Zero ranks the whole candidate pool using evidence already saved in the shared cache. Each of these twenty seven candidates has less than twenty percent known coverage, so the first screen protects them all. An included route is eligible for another evidence round. It is not a driving recommendation.

title: Calculate the exact first cost
narration: Five new lookups per route would exceed the current batch limit, so I set the quota to three. I also briefly deselect and reselect a candidate to show the estimate respond. The free cache check then finds twenty six unique, uncached cells. At one credit and one cent per new lookup, this round is capped at twenty six cents. I start it only after seeing that exact count.

title: Watch the first evidence round
narration: The first RentCast round is underway. Each returned cell updates every route that shares it. The twenty six calls succeed, and the app reranks all twenty seven candidates. The next included pool narrows to eleven routes. Unknown cells remain unknown; the app does not treat them as low-value cells.

title: Compare and run another round
narration: Here I compare the new route cards. Distance, travel time, known coverage, and weighted price per square foot all matter. The next free check identifies fourteen new shared-cell lookups. After those fourteen calls finish, seven routes remain included. An excluded route can reenter if later evidence changes the ranking.

title: Inspect a map point
narration: The map shows the selected route, its colored property cells, and the highway segments excluded from the property comparison. I also inspect a cell away from the candidate route. That single extra lookup is clearly identified as outside the route, so it does not change the route rankings.

title: Narrow the pool again
narration: The third evidence plan calls for ten new cells. I review the separate Run control, then let the requests finish. The included pool falls from seven to four. All four rounds keep the culling percentage at thirty five percent, with whole-route rounding shown in the interface.

title: Reach two finalists
narration: One more exact plan uses nine new lookups. When it completes, two routes are included and twenty five are excluded from further sampling. The shorter finalist is sixty six point three four miles and seventy five and a half minutes. It has about eighty one percent known cell coverage and six unknown cells.

title: Review before choosing
narration: I move into Look around and select a known route cell for inspection. Street View can add visual context, but its imagery date matters, and the property value signal is not a safety verdict. The recording ends at this review point; a route choice should follow your own inspection and current road conditions.
